---
title: "simstim rewind"
---

<!-- Generated by `just docs` from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

List disk checkpoints or return to one.

```text
simstim rewind <host>/<session> [<n>] [flags]
```

Lists a microvm sandbox's disk checkpoints, newest first, numbered from 1. Choose a number to restore its files and conversation. Rewind makes an undo checkpoint first, then starts the sandbox cold. Without a number it asks at a terminal. Reflink support is required on the host.

## Examples

```sh
simstim rewind box/auth-fix --list
simstim rewind box/auth-fix 2 -y
```

## Flags

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | print JSON for scripts, and ask nothing (see docs/how-to/scripting.md) |
| `--list` | list checkpoints without restoring one |
| `--secret <list>` | pass again secrets that the sandbox needs and that hosts.toml does not give its host |
| `-y`, `--yes` | answer yes to every question: restore the selected checkpoint |

## Flags from the parent command

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--debug[=<categories>]` | turn on the debug mode, with every category, or with the categories listed: attach, net, memory, launcher, runtime. A list binds only in the = form, such as `--debug=net` |
| `--debug-file <file>` | write the client's debug records to this file. On its own, it turns on every category (SIMSTIM_DEBUG_FILE does the same) |
| `--no-color` | print no colour (NO_COLOR does the same) |
| `--no-input` | ask nothing: a question that needs an answer fails with exit code 4, and names the flag that answers it (SIMSTIM_NO_INPUT=1 does the same) |
